title: Postmortem: silent observability gap caused autoscale saturation in console routing
creator: Amira Patel
description:
Summary: During a gradual customer traffic increase on 2025-11-02 we observed a prolonged degradation of console request throughput for a subset of tenants which did not trigger our usual autoscaling or alerting. The symptom was increased 95th/99th tail latency on the console route, intermittent 503s for admin requests, and progressive queue growth on a small set of scheduler pods. The incident was not detected by existing dashboards because key signals were missing and several dashboard panels aggregated across tenants, masking a tenant-level saturation pattern. This ticket captures the postmortem findings and concrete action items to close the observability blind spots that allowed the condition to persist.

Impact: partial console degradation for ~3 hours affecting ~4 tenants during low-traffic hours. No customer data loss. Increased latency impacted internal rollout tasks and a small number of API calls for dedicated customers.

Root cause hypothesis (consolidated): 1) Autoscaler decisions relied on aggregated ingress RPS and pod CPU which did not reflect per-tenant queue depth or KV cache eviction pressure; 2) The KV cache adoption increased tail latency for requests that missed the prefix cache due to hidden eviction spikes; 3) Dashboards rolled up metrics across shards and tenants so the skewed tenant was not visible; 4) Trace sampling configuration excluded long-running scheduler and cache-eviction spans.

Immediate mitigation taken: scaled up dedicated scheduler pool to relieve queue backlog, increased trace sampling for console route to 100% for 30 minutes to capture traces, and created temporary Grafana panels with tenant filters for the affected tenants.

Evidence & artifacts:
- Incident timeline (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/console-incidents/2025-11-02-autoscale-saturation
- Root-cause traces (sample): https://jaeger.redwood.ai/trace/abcd1234 (access internal)
- Temporary dashboard snapshots: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/console/adhoc-tenant-slices
- Related PR for quick fixes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4123
comments: 2025-11-03 - Amira Patel: Initial postmortem draft, assigned to Jonas for action planning. Noting that our production autoscaler doesn't ingest queue_depth_per_tenant metrics and that prefix_cache.hit_ratio is only emitted at a shard level.

2025-11-04 - Jonas Becker: Reproduced eviction spike in staging using synthetic traffic. Confirmed that kv_cache.evictions_per_min is emitted but not routed into the console metrics pipeline for tenant-scoped aggregation. Opening ENG-82721 to add ingestion path.

2025-11-05 - Priya Nair (SRE): Added a temporary alert rule in prod to fire when any tenant's scheduler_queue_depth > 500 for 5m. Alert linked to oncall playbook so humans can scale before autoscaler triggers. Playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/playbooks/console-queue-backlog

2025-11-06 - Jonas Becker: Submitted prototype PR to change trace sampling for scheduler spans and to add a KV-cache eviction span tag: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/128. Requesting design review from UX metrics team for dashboard placement.

2025-11-08 - Amira Patel: PM review - please ensure customer impact notes and communications are added to the incident doc before we close. Also coordinate with Dedicated capacity product team if any SLA language needs adjusting.

2025-11-10 - Jonas Becker: Updated action items list and schedule for phased rollout; marking instrumentation and dashboard work as highest priority. Will follow up with the Dataserv team on ingestion backlog capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant scheduler_queue_depth metric is ingested to metrics pipeline and appears as a dimension in Grafana within staging by 2025-11-14
New KV-cache metrics (kv_cache.evictions_per_min, kv_cache.prefix_miss_ratio) emitted per-tenant and visible in console dashboards
At least three new dashbaord panels (sharded+tenant) that surface 95th/99th tail latency, queue depth, and kv-cache eviction rate with tenant filter enabled
Alerting: production rule that triggers when any tenant queue depth > 500 sustained for 5m and a secondary alert for prefix_cache.hit_ratio < 60% for 10m
Tracing: scheduler and kv-cache eviction spans are sampled at 100% in staging and 10% in production with long-span retention for 7 days
Runbook updated with step-by-step mitigation (scale quickstart, temporary shard draining) and smoke-test checklist
action_items: ENG-82721 - Instrumentation: Add tenant dimensions for kv_cache.evictions_per_min, prefix_cache.hit_ratio, and scheduler_queue_depth. Owner: Jonas Becker. Estimate: 3. Due: 2025-11-14.

ENG-82722 - Metrics pipeline: Add route to ingest new tenant-scoped metrics and increase ingestion capacity for burst windows. Owner: Dataserv team (contact: Priya Nair). Estimate: 5. Due: 2025-11-18.

ENG-82723 - Dashboards: Create new console observability dashboard with per-tenant filtering and clear 99th panels; replace the existing aggregated-only view. Owner: Miguel Torres (Observability UX). Estimate: 3. Due: 2025-11-16.
ENG-82724 - Alerts & Runbook: Implement production alert rules and update the console runbook with escalation steps and mitigations. Owner: SRE (Priya Nair). Estimate: 2. Due: 2025-11-12.
ENG-82725 - Tracing: Adjust sampling rules to capture scheduler and cache eviction spans; add trace span tags for tenant_id and eviction_reason. Owner: Jonas Becker. Estimate: 2. Due: 2025-11-12.

ENG-82726 - Post-deploy verification: Run a staged chaos test that simulates tenant-skewed traffic and validate alerts + dashboards fire as expected. Owner: QA (Elena Griggs). Estimate: 2. Due: 2025-11-20.
ENG-82727 - Communication: Draft customer-facing incident summary and internal blameless retrospective. Owner: Amira Patel. Estimate: 1. Due: 2025-11-11.
notes: Design trade-offs: adding per-tenant cardinality to metrics increases storage and query cost. Proposal is to emit per-tenant metrics only for known high-risk namespaces and provide sampling/rollup for low-volume tenants.
Operational constraint: ingestion pipeline changes require a short maintenance window to increase throughput. Dataserv estimates 2 hours of deploy time with a quick rollback plan.
Follow-ups after action items: schedule a 30-day SLO review to ensure no recurrence and measure alert noise.
Related learning: rely less on aggregated CPU for autoscaling decisions; drive autoscaler by queue_depth or request backlog percentiles for console routes.
